corrections.text: The Implications section says "The Harvard data ends in March 2026 and the survey was fielded from April to June 2026, so the two do not cover the same months." That holds for the version of the Harvard paper that Ars Technica and TechRadar covered (dated August 4, 2026: about 300 million work events, about 700 firms, January 2021 to March 2026, which matches the article's Harvard figures). The version now on the authors' site, dated November 9, 2026, reports 445 million work events at 655 firms from January 2021 to August 2026 and different estimates (for example, AI agents +44.0% lines of code and review time +56.1%), so its data period overlaps the survey's fielding. The article did not cite or check the paper.

The article says AI agents were responsible for "23.3 percent of review comments and 10.8 percent of pull requests", following Ars Technica's wording. The paper (both versions) says 23.3% of all review comments are generated by AI and 10.8% of pull requests receive at least one AI-generated comment; it does not describe these as pull requests written by AI agents.

In the Google section, "83 percent of those actions" repeats the post's wording "Over 4 in 5 of those actions (83% sessions)", which uses both "actions" and "sessions" for the same figure, and the 70, 77 and 105 percent "per session" figures are given without a stated comparison group (the post does not say what they are measured against). The Implications line that Google's figures "come from a regression" applies only to those three figures; the 13, 6, 83, 41 and 57 percent figures are descriptive shares of traces.
